title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution (LP-FT)
mechanism: A random head distorts features during full fine-tuning; training the head first on frozen features (LP) then fine-tuning (FT) preserves them.
adaptation: PF already freezes the encoder 1k steps. Open variant: LP phase until the decoder converges (about 5k steps) then full FT at house lr, to separate LP-first from low encoder lr.
evidence: 10 shift datasets: FT +2% ID, -7% OOD vs LP; LP-FT +1% ID, +10% OOD vs FT.
min_experiment: Arm LP5k-FT(house lr) vs PF and house, seeds 5-9. Metric: E1 inactive IoU, test relF1@2. Kill if not above house on E1 inactive.
prior_overlap: Largely tested: PF is an LP-FT-like recipe (1k frozen steps plus 0.1x lr) and won E1 inactive. Only the split of LP length and post-LP lr is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: PF already does 1k frozen steps. Open variant: frozen phase until decoder converges (5k steps), then full fine-tune at the house lr (not 0.1x), to separate LP-first from low encoder lr.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: LP 5k + FT at 1e-3, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF and house. Metric: E1 inactive IoU, layer3/4 cosine to init, test crack relF1@2. Kill: E1 inactive not above house by +0.05 (then low lr, not LP, is PF's active part).
